recognize_zh: 大小正常的紅血球內有兩個成熟的滋養體/早期裂殖體，胞內含深褐黑色瘧色素（hemozoin）與數個染色質點；感染的紅血球沒有變大、也沒有 Schüffner 小點，符合惡性瘧原蟲（P. falciparum）。
features: Two parasitized red cells containing compact mature trophozoites/early schizonts with dark brown-black hemozoin pigment
Parasites show several chromatin dots and bluish cytoplasm filling part of the host cell
Infected red cells are normal in size, without Schüffner stippling
Background of densely packed, uninfected red cells; no gametocytes or white cells in field
describe_en: Smear from a bone marrow aspirate preparation (thin, erythrocyte-rich area) shows two parasitized red cells containing pigmented mature trophozoites/early schizonts with coarse dark hemozoin and several chromatin dots. The infected erythrocytes are not enlarged and lack Schüffner stippling. No gametocytes are present in this field, and marrow cellular elements are not included. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium falciparum infection with mature (pigmented) asexual forms, which are typically sequestered in tissue and marrow rather than circulating.

ddx.vs: Vivax and ovale mature forms enlarge the host red cell and show Schüffner stippling, whereas these infected cells are normal-sized without stippling.
P. malariae shows band-form trophozoites and rosette schizonts in small red cells, and species confirmation may require PCR when only pigmented trophozoites are seen.
Babesia lacks hemozoin pigment and schizonts and may form Maltese-cross tetrads.
